item.title: Province seeks Islanders’ input on seasonal time change
item.description:
Province seeks Islanders’ input on seasonal time change jenniferdhogan Tue, 11/03/2026 - 16:03

The Government of Prince Edward Island is inviting Islanders to share their views on whether the province should continue changing its clocks twice a year. 

Islanders can complete the online survey at PEITimeChange.ca until December 13, 2026. The survey asks whether they prefer to keep the current system or move to year-round standard time or year-round daylight-saving time.

“Across Canada, provinces are taking a closer look at whether changing the clocks twice a year still makes sense. It’s a conversation worth having here on Prince Edward Island. How we observe time affects everything from our daily routines to how we do business with our neighbours. Before making any decisions, we want to hear what Islanders think and understand what matters most to them.”

- Premier Rob Lantz

The survey will also seek feedback on factors that may influence people’s preferences, including daylight hours, work and school schedules, and potential impacts on businesses and communities.

The feedback will help the province better understand Islanders’ priorities and inform further discussions with the other maritime provinces. 

Prince Edward Island currently observes daylight saving time from March to November, when clocks are moved forward by one hour, and standard time during the winter months. Moving to a year-round system would eliminate the twice-yearly clock changes but would also affect how much daylight people experience during the morning and evening hours.

item.title: Legislative Assembly returns to Province House for the fall sitting
item.description:
Legislative Assembly returns to Province House for the fall sitting jenniferdhogan Tue, 11/03/2026 - 09:36

The Legislative Assembly of Prince Edward Island will return to the newly restored Province House when the fall sitting begins on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

The return marks the first time Members of the Legislative Assembly will sit in the historic Legislative Chamber since 2014, following more than a decade of restoration and conservation work.

“Returning to Province House is an important moment for our province and our democracy. This building has been part of our country’s history for generations, and it is fitting that the work of representing Islanders will once again take place here. My government is ready to get back to work and continue taking action on the priorities that matter most to Islanders.”

-  Premier Rob Lantz

The fall sitting will build on the priorities outlined in the government’s spring Speech from the Throne and Operating Budget, including improving access to healthcare, addressing affordability, strengthening energy security and protecting Island land. 

A key legislative priority will be changes to the Island Regulatory and Appeals Commission (IRAC), following the independent review led by Commissioner Rory Francis. Government has committed to introducing legislation to replace IRAC with two specialized bodies, the PEI Energy and Utilities Board and the PEI Land and Appeals Board, to strengthen transparency, accountability and public confidence in regulatory decisions. 

Additional legislation expected to be introduced during the fall sitting includes amendments to the Gasoline Tax Act to address the suspension of the provincial fuel tax, a new Coroners Act and Correctional Services Act legislation to modernize public safety frameworks, and a new Good Samaritan Act to make clear that people who help in an emergency are protected from liability. 

Government will also table its 2027-2028 Capital Budget, outlining foundational investment in healthcare, schools, energy and the roads and bridges that connect Island communities.  

“Islanders expect their government to focus on the issues that affect their daily lives,” said Premier Rob Lantz. “We have important work ahead of us, from improving access to primary care and addressing affordability concerns to planning our energy future. This sitting is another opportunity to move the work forward and deliver results for Islanders.”

With the reopening of Province House, Islanders are encouraged to attend legislative proceedings in the historic Chamber. Members of the public can watch from the public gallery during the following sitting hours:

  • Tuesday to Thursday: 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m.
  • Friday: 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

Proceedings are also broadcasted live online at assembly.pe.ca.

item.title: Province strengthens Wetland Conservation Policy
item.description:
Province strengthens Wetland Conservation Policy jenniferdhogan Mon, 11/02/2026 - 16:01

Updates to the province's Wetland Conservation Policy will strengthen the Island’s wetland protection by providing clearer requirements, greater transparency and more consistent decision-making. 

The updated policy sets out clear requirements, options, and rates for wetland compensation when impacts cannot be avoided. It also provides greater certainty for landowners and developers while maintaining the province's commitment to protecting wetlands.

"Prince Edward Island's wetlands are an important part of our natural environment, helping protect water quality, reduce flooding and support biodiversity. These changes reinforce our commitment to protecting these valuable resources while making the decision-making process clearer and more transparent.  Islanders deserve a clear understanding of the requirements and a transparent approach to wetland conservation."

- Premier Rob Lantz

The updated policy establishes:

  • Clear compensation options: formalized requirements that allow restoration or creation of wetlands at a 3:1 replacement ratio or contribute to the province's Wetland Protection Fund.
  • Consistent compensation rates: a rate of $60,000 per acre for unavoidable wetland impacts, reflecting existing restoration costs and compensation practices.
  • Flexibility for minor impacts: a limited exemption from compensation requirements for minor wetland impacts, reducing costs for small-scale development projects.
  • Greater clarity and transparency: clearer guidance on compensation requirements to support consistent decision-making.

"These updates strengthen the policy by formally establishing compensation requirements that have been used for many years and provide a clearer framework for decision-making," said Minister of Land and Environment Darlene Compton. "Our priority remains avoiding impacts to wetlands wherever possible while ensuring there are clear and consistent requirements when impacts cannot be avoided."

Introduced in 2003, the Wetland Conservation Policy supports the province's commitment to preventing a net loss of wetland habitat. Compensation collected through the Wetland Protection Fund supports wetland restoration and creation projects across Prince Edward Island.

The province continues to provide mapping tools and resources to help landowners and developers identify potential wetlands early in the planning process. As wetlands may exist in areas not identified through mapping, site assessments are an important part of determining whether development restrictions apply.

To review the updated policy, visit Wetland Identification | Government of Prince Edward Island.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
